chapters.summary: Ask an average group of investors if they are interested in understanding market expectations, and you’ll hear a resounding yes. But if you ask them how they go about reading the market, they’ll probably fall back on a slew of contemporaneous, statistical benchmarks such as short-term earnings and price-earnings multiples. Though ubiquitous, these investment shorthands simply don’t paint an economically sound picture of today’s expectations because they aren’t reliably linked to shareholder value. As Warren Buffett says, “Forecasts usually tell us more of the forecaster than of the future.” 1 Where, then, do you turn? We start with our primary interest, which is to identify when buyback announcements offer a credible signal to revise expectations. We go on to present a golden rule that we can use to evaluate all buyback programs.
